notes: ACCESS: robots.txt (www.zarahome.com/robots.txt) has no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-* entry and no blanket Disallow: / for User-agent: *, so all tiers were permitted. Tier (a) plain HTTP GET hit an Akamai Bot Manager JS interstitial (bm-verify challenge) on / and on itxrest API calls made outside a browser session (403 Service Unavailable). Escalated to tier (b) Playwright Chromium headless=False with --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled (same pattern that worked for SR21/90/106/117 Zara Home storefronts) - this cleared the interstitial on first try; tier (c) Claude-in-Chrome was not needed. TREE: the site is an Angular-Universal SSR app (Inditex 'itxrest' backend). No <a href> subcategory links exist in the static DOM; the full mega-menu category tree is embedded as JSON in the page's Angular TransferState cache under the key '/api/storefront/1/stores/84009901/menu?language=fr-FR...'. That JSON (41 top-level nodes, ~750 nodes total incl. editorial/recipe noise) was extracted and parsed to enumerate every node's name, seo keyword/seoId (-> canonical URL) and children. Many menu 'children' are color/material filter chips that reuse the exact same URL as their parent (e.g. Couettes 'Microfibre'/'Plume et duvet' all resolve to chambre-couettes-n956) - these were collapsed into a single leaf row, not treated as distinct subcategories. QTY: Zara Home category pages render no visible 'N articles' count text, so quantity was read from the site's own itxrest product-listing API (same endpoint the page itself calls), field path productIds array length, called live from within the authenticated browser tab via fetch() (showProducts=false&showNoStock=false&withSubCategories=false). Verified this is a true category total, not a fixed page-size cap, by confirming a small niche category (Cache-sommiers) returned 6 and a large one (Serviettes de bain) returned 135 - both well off any round cap; also confirmed page/offset params had no effect (full list always returned). The site's own top-level 'chambre-n944' page is itself a curated 'TOP 100' bestsellers view (per its gridContext.sectionNames), not a real category - it and all other top-level room pages were bypassed in favor of their real subcategory nodes. EXCLUDED (View All / duplicate-URL / non-product-category, per rules 27/25): 'Tapis' parent nav node (salon-tapis-tout-n4121) resolved to a dead 'Page d'erreur'; its 'Tout afficher' sibling (decoration-tapis-salon-n992, 115 items) is a real page but is the View-All for the 9 distinct rug-material subcategories that were kept instead. 'Nappes/Tout afficher' (salle-a-manger-linge-de-table-n1034, 237 items, title 'Linge de table et nappes') and kids 'Draps/Tout afficher' (enfants-vetements-lit-n1097, 161 items, title 'Linge de lit pour enfants') both share their menu id with an explicit 'Tout afficher' sibling in the tree JSON, so were treated as View-All umbrellas and dropped in favor of their genuinely distinct-URL children. 'Corbeilles de chambre' (chambre-corbeilles-n4648) returned the identical qty (35) and identical first products as 'Corbeilles et paniers' (decoration-paniers-n997) - kept only the latter as a duplicate-content alias. EXCLUDED (not Textile/Storage per rules boundary): 'Buanderie' (entretien-vetements-n1399, Soin du linge) - checked; dominant content is ironing boards, drying racks and a laundry pot, i.e. laundry-care equipment (rule storage.md #30 excludes tools like this), even though it also contains one cotton laundry bag - not extracted since the category's primary content is non-storage equipment. 'Rangements' under the Meubles/Furniture top nav (meubles-rangement-n4111) excluded per storage.md #21 (explicitly under the Furniture menu -> Furniture task, not this one). Kids/baby apparel, toys, tableware, fragrance, pet collection, editorials/recipes, gift cards and all curated collection/bestseller/sale pages were excluded as out of scope. FLAGS: 'Rideaux, voilages et stores' includes a curtain rod (hardware) alongside real curtains - kept at MEDIUM since curtains dominate. 'Peignoirs et chaussons' mixes bathrobes (Textile) with slippers (apparel) in one page - kept at MEDIUM, name reflects the mix. 'Porte-serviettes et crochets' mixes towel racks with coat hooks and a toilet-paper holder - kept at LOW per storage.md #19's explicit 'Towel Storage Racks' inclusion, flagged for review. 'Couvre-lits' (59) and 'Couvre-lits d'ete' (39), and 'Edredons' (30) and 'Couettes d'hiver' (0), were each kept as two sibling rows rather than collapsed - the specific/seasonal child has a materially different, non-superset product count from its general parent, so both are genuine distinct listing pages, not View-All duplicates.
